branch: ك و ن Quranic usage: مَكَان / مَكَانَة
after: a faint place or standing resonance
reason: The usage list includes مَكَان and مَكَانَة, while the nearby مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ supplies a place image. This repeats the location echo already captured more directly under R09.B002.1.

after: their past state is set against the coming event-day
reason: The focus وَكَانُوا۟ places their discernment in a past state, while 29:36 urges its audience toward ٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلْءَاخِرَ. That event-time cue lightly sharpens the dictionary's sense of being present within time, though the auxiliary's ordinary past-state meaning remains dominant.

after: positive being faintly answers a negated copula elsewhere in the surah
reason: The rhetorical أَوَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ is a negated copula, not an exception here. Its explicit being-versus-not-being wording gives a weak contrastive cue for B001's broad occurrence sense beside the focus's affirmative وَكَانُوا۟.

after: their past state is viewed against the Day of Judgment
reason: Fatiha's يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ supplies another event-day cue for the same temporal contrast recorded at R09.B001.4. It does not add a distinct branch image.

after: an exclusionary frame faintly colors their state
reason: Fatiha's غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ is a real exclusion expression, matching the branch's dictionary note that a dependent form of ك و ن can mark exception. No exception is stated with وَكَانُوا۟ itself, so the daily recited phrase supplies only a faint resonance.

after: the temporal state meets an event-day frame
reason: The bridge pairs another كَانُوا۟ with ٱلْيَوْمَ, repeating the time-and-state relation already recorded at R09.B001.4. It does not supply a separate image for the focus.

after: they had been in a place or settled state, now exposed by their dwellings
reason: ك و ن B002 gives a rare place or position sense, and the focus itself places وَكَانُوا۟ beside the explicit dwelling word مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ. Their former being can faintly carry a sense of being-in-place as the dwellings survive to testify, while the plain copula remains clear.

after: a people's state is lightly grounded in where they dwell
reason: The address يَٰقَوْمِ in 29:36 is followed by ٱلْأَرْضِ, giving its community a concrete setting. That place cue weakly activates KWN's residence or location branch beside the focus's past-state verb.

after: the people are situated in a settlement
reason: ٱلْقَرْيَةِ supplies the same settlement-location cue represented more directly by R09.B002.6. The descent wording مُنزِلُونَ does not add another position image.

after: their state can be faintly heard against the inhabitants' settled place
reason: In 29:34, مُنزِلُونَ is directed upon أَهْلِ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ, explicitly locating a people in a town. This settlement cue offers a weaker parallel to the focus's وَكَانُوا۟ and its dwellings than the local word captured at R09.B002.1.

after: their being faintly takes a locative cast
reason: The concept route reaches ٱلْأَرْضِ, another place cue, and therefore repeats the location reading already supported by the focus's مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ at R09.B002.1.

after: their state sits faintly beside a straight course or position
reason: The Fatiha's ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ gives a spatial course rather than a dwelling. It weakly activates the branch's place or position facet next to وَكَانُوا۟, without making the focus mean that they stood on the guided path.

after: their state carries a faint rank or standing resonance
reason: The phrase أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ marks the guided people as specially favored, which can suggest a standing or rank beside KWN's place-and-status branch. The focus does not itself state such a rank, so this remains a note.

after: the former inhabitants' place remains as a sign, echoing the focus's dwelling testimony
reason: In 29:31, the people of the town are described with كَانُوا۟, and 29:35 says مِنْهَآ ءَايَةً بَيِّنَةً, a clear sign was left from it. This nearby ruin pattern makes the place branch more than a bare location: the state of a people is tied to a settlement that remains as evidence, anticipating the focus's مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ.

after: their state carries a faint sense of responsibility for what they did
reason: The focus calls the deeds أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ, explicitly assigning the works to them. That ownership supplies a weak responsibility cue for KWN's undertaking or guarantee branch, though it does not say that they vouched for another person.

after: help sought from another faintly resembles undertaken support
reason: The Fatiha's نَسْتَعِينُ evokes support, but that is the same broad responsibility-and-support association already noted for owned deeds at R09.B003.1. It does not add a separate guarantee image.

after: their ruined habitation faintly suggests subjection
reason: The focus's مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ names dwellings and, in context, the homes are the surviving evidence of a defeated people. That aftermath weakly calls KWN's dictionary sense of yielding or abasement, although the word itself means dwellings rather than submission.

after: their state is heard against the call to submit in worship
reason: The focus وَكَانُوا۟ closes the account of people diverted from the way, while 29:36 explicitly commands another community, ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ. That command activates KWN's dictionary branch of yielding and submission, making the focus's claim that they were perceptive ring against the submission they failed to follow.

after: formal worship suggests submission
reason: ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ is another worship cue for subjection, already represented more directly by the command ٱعْبُدُوا۟ at R09.B004.4. It adds no separate submission point.

after: servanthood can be heard as yielding
reason: The address يَٰعِبَادِىَ names servanthood, which repeats the submission cue already captured under R09.B004.4. Its later placement does not give a distinct branch image.

after: their state is measured against the truth everyone must submit to
reason: The statement كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ presents death as unavoidable for every soul. That universal limit weakly activates the branch image of yielding to what cannot be resisted, coloring the focus's past state without changing its plain grammar.

after: the daily pledge names worshipful submission
reason: Fatiha's نَعْبُدُ directly names the same worshipful yielding as R09.B004.4's ٱعْبُدُوا۟. The daily recitation reinforces that point but does not create a second one.

after: religion evokes obedient submission
reason: ٱلدِّينِ can carry obedience, but that submission association is already supported more plainly by ٱعْبُدُوا۟ at R09.B004.4. This line supplies no distinct image.

after: the worship command again supplies a yielding cue
reason: The bridge returns to ٱعْبُدُوا۟ as its submission trigger, the same cue recorded at R09.B004.4. It does not add a new reading of وَكَانُوا۟.

after: a bad condition faintly shadows the state
reason: In 29:33, سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ describes distress at the visitors' arrival, calling the bad-condition part of KWN B006. No night is named, so the dictionary's specific overnight situation is only partly activated and remains a note.

after: bad deeds evoke the bad-condition facet
reason: سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ gives a general badness cue, but it repeats only the weak bad-condition facet already recorded from the more direct distress word سِىٓءَ at R09.B006.4. It does not supply the missing night element.

after: the concept route points to distress
reason: The concept path reaches وَضَاقَ in the same distress scene as R09.B006.4. That repeats the weak bad-condition cue and still does not call the branch's night image.

after: the bad-state concept reaches the Lot scene
reason: This second concept route also terminates at سِىٓءَ, so it duplicates the condition cue retained in R09.B006.4. The route has no independent nighttime trigger.

after: the bridge carries the same distress image
reason: The bridge uses 29:33's سِىٓءَ as its bad-condition pole, repeating R09.B006.4's trigger. It does not add the overnight circumstance required for a stronger reading.

branch: ب ي ن / ب ص ر — clarity and insight echo
after: their insight stands beside what has become clear from their dwellings
reason: The focus pairs تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ with مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, placing public clarity beside the people's own insight. Their dwellings now make the outcome clear to the audience, even though these people had perception and were turned away from the path.
